cards.explanation: The answer is a prostitute named Rahab. The spies went into Jericho and stayed at the house of a woman named Rahab, and the text calls her a prostitute plainly. It doesn't say why they picked her door, so I won't guess. Keep her name handy, friends, because she's about to be the hero of this whole chapter.

The answer is that the king tells her to bring the men out to him. He sends word to Rahab: “Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house…” He even gives his reason, which is that they have come to spy out the whole land. That's a short order with a lot riding on it.

The answer is False. The woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She tells the king's men, “Yes, the men did come to me…” and then says she did not know where they had come from. Admitting half the story while the spies are hidden? I bet that was a long few minutes for her.

The answer is that she tells them to pursue the spies quickly. She says, “Pursue them quickly, and you may catch them!” She sends the king's men running off after men who are really up on her roof. That's a whole lot of confidence in one sentence.

The answer is True. The king's men set out along the road to the fords of the Jordan, and the moment they were out, the gate was shut. I think that's a very quick door. Rahab's rooftop plan had good timing, friends, and the men she hid were still safe under the flax (Joshua 2:6).

The answer is that the LORD has given Israel the land. Rahab tells the spies, “I know that the LORD has given you this land…” She says it plainly, up on her own roof. Keep an ear out, friends, because she's just getting warmed up.

The answer is True. Rahab tells the spies that the fear of them has fallen on the people, “…so that all who dwell in the land are melting in fear of you.” Picture a whole city with the same knot in its stomach. She says it straight to the spies on her roof, and her words cover everyone in the land.

The answer is that Israel devoted them to destruction. Rahab says Israel devoted Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites across the Jordan, to destruction. That's part of what Jericho has heard. The news had traveled a long way before the spies ever got there.

The answer is that He is God in heaven above and on earth below. Rahab says, “…for the LORD your God is God in the heavens above and on the earth below.” That's a big thing to say about God from a rooftop in Jericho. Those are her words, friends, and I think they're worth slowing down for.

The answer is family. Rahab asks the spies to spare her father and mother, her brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them. She had just hidden two strangers, and now she asks for something for the people she loves. I think that tells you a lot about her heart. She also asks for a sure sign, so she's asking for more than a quick promise.

The answer is True. The men agree, “Our lives for your lives!” They add, “If you do not report our mission, we will show you kindness and faithfulness when the LORD gives us the land.” So her silence is part of the deal.
The answer is a rope. Rahab's house is built into the city wall, so she let the spies down through the window by a rope. No front door and no street. I get nervous just standing on a counter edge.

The answer is the hill country. Rahab tells the spies to go there so their pursuers will not find them. She had just let them down by a rope, and she sent them off with directions. That's one thoughtful host, I think.

The answer is until their pursuers have returned. Rahab says to hide in the hill country for three days until the pursuers have returned, and then go on their way. Her plan has a clear finish line. Hide, wait, and then go.

The answer is a scarlet cord. The spies say she must have tied this scarlet cord in the window she let them down through. It's one of the conditions they set for the oath. A little red cord with a big job.

The answer is True. The spies say she must have brought her father and mother and brothers and all her family into her house. That's the second condition. The cord and the family both come before the oath holds.
The answer is that she agrees to their terms. Rahab says, “Let it be as you say…” No haggling, no extra rounds. She agrees and sends them away.

The answer is False. Rahab said, “Let it be as you say…” and sent them away. And when they had gone, she tied the scarlet cord in the window. The text puts the cord in her window once the spies were gone, with no waiting for Israel to arrive.

The answer is True. The spies stayed in the hill country three days, until their pursuers had returned without finding them. The pursuers had searched all along the road. That's a lot of road to cover and still come back empty-handed.

The answer is that the LORD has delivered the entire land into their hands. The spies tell Joshua, “The LORD has surely delivered the entire land into our hands…” They add that all who dwell in the land are melting in fear of them. That's the same thing Rahab told them on the roof.
